defaults.name: Sandbox JS
defaults.trust: v1 = trusted maker apps, no untrusted-code isolation promise
defaults.home: sandbox-kernel/js/ on a feature branch, no new repository
defaults.profiles: DOM-lite UI profile included; Game-Maker profile stays with gamemaker-os
defaults.note: Defaults chosen 2026-11-13 for Lewis; he can change any of them.

entries.js: fs.open(path) -> FileHandle {size, position, read(n), readInto(view, off, n), text(n), seek(pos), close()}; fs.readBytes(path); fs.stat(path); fs.readFile
entries.test: host: open existing/missing/too-long path; 16-handle exhaustion
entries.notes: Handles are generation-tagged; stale fd gives EBADF. 16 handles shared by all kinds (the table keeps 12 for the app). The size comes from the parent folder's entry (the kernel has no stat).

entries.js: fs.createWriter(path) / fs.write(path, data): staged in the app's memory, published by one whole-file write at commit()
entries.errors: EACCES (no capability), EROFS (outside the app's cache or save path), EINVAL and ENAMETOOLONG (8.3 rules), EBUSY (another writer, or a reader open in the save area), ENOSPC, EDQUOT
entries.test: tests/files_run.py: names and scope, one writer, quota, abort at stop
entries.notes: 8.3 names only, uppercased by the runtime. One writer at a time, in JS too. The app's own quota (default 256 KiB, jsrt_write_quota) is checked before the kernel's 1 MiB limit.

entries.js: fs.createWriter('/sd/OS/SAVES/<id>/NAME.EXT') / fs.write(path, data)
entries.errors: as cache plus EDQUOT (-122) past 64 game folders or 32 files per game
entries.test: tests/files_run.py: 33rd file and 65th folder EDQUOT, full card ENOSPC
entries.notes: The id is the app's folder name. 64 game folders and 32 files per game are the kernel's (EDQUOT, tested against a host model).

entries.js: console.log/info/warn/error -> one write per line
entries.test: host: line longer than 120 bytes is cut; control bytes become ?
entries.notes: Each write is one log line of up to 120 chars; trailing newline dropped. USB log shows OS: prefix.

entries.js: screen.lease({width,height,depth}) -> ScreenLease (one at a time, JSRT_H_DISPLAY); screen.setMode unchanged (page modes)
entries.test: host: second open EBUSY
entries.notes: The page (DOM-lite) opens the device at start; a lease is exclusive with it: the page stops drawing, setMode and play() are refused (EBUSY) until release().

entries.js: input.open() -> InputQueue (JSRT_H_INPUT, 4 at most) with on(key|attach|detach|reset); document keydown/keyup unchanged
entries.errors: EACCES (not read-only), EINVAL (blocking open), EBUSY (second reader), ENODEV
entries.test: host: blocking open EINVAL; second reader EBUSY
entries.notes: The runtime owns the one kernel reader (EBUSY for a second); queues fan its events out in JS. The device is reopened every 100 ms after it goes away.

entries.js: audio.open({rate, channels, onneed, targetMs}) -> AudioOut (JSRT_H_AUDIO, one per app); rate 8000..48000 dividing 48000, channels 1 or 2
entries.test: host: second writer EBUSY; read access EACCES
entries.notes: The kernel format is fixed (stereo S16, 48 kHz); the runtime doubles mono and repeats samples for a lower rate. ENOENT from a kernel older than 1.8 is reported as ENODEV. A second open in the same app is EBUSY before the kernel is asked.

entries.js: eink.open() -> Eink or null; eink.available (false without a panel)
entries.test: devices_run.py EinkOpen
entries.notes: ENODEV (no panel, or a kernel older than 1.9) gives null, not a throw. One owner per app; the handle (JSRT_H_EINK) is released at stop and the kernel gets its screen back with a clear when an update may go then. close() keeps the page up, release() clears.

entries.js: serial.open({mode: 'r'|'w'|'rw'}) -> SerialPort
entries.errors: EINVAL (blocking open or access mode 3), EBUSY, ENODEV
entries.test: devices_run.py SerialTests
entries.notes: The runtime always opens nonblocking, so a blocking open (EINVAL) cannot be asked for. Direction is enforced by the runtime (the kernel does not). Hardware-untested per docs/os-authors.md.

entries.js: FileHandle.read(into, offset?) ; InputQueue.read(); SerialPort.read(into)
entries.errors: EAGAIN -> returns 0 bytes / null, EBADF, EINVAL (input count < 16), EFAULT
entries.test: host: each device kind; count > 1 MiB EINVAL
entries.notes: Files (slice 4a): one read is at most 256 KiB in JS and 1 MiB in the kernel. The input device (slice 4b) is read inside the runtime, at most 128 events a turn, never by the app; serial binds in 4d. Slice 4d: SerialPort.read(into) takes at most 4096 bytes, 0 when empty; the 'data' event reads at most 256 bytes at a time and 1024 a turn.

entries.js: Writer.write(bytes); AudioOut.write(pcm) -> frames queued; SerialPort.write(bytes); Eink.page(bytes)
entries.errors: EAGAIN (audio ring full -> returns 0 frames), EINVAL (audio not 4-byte frames; eink not 3904 bytes), ENOSPC (cache > 1 MiB)
entries.test: host: partial audio write; eink wrong size
entries.notes: Audio and serial writes can be partial or dropped; the JS wrapper returns counts, never loops silently. Slice 4c: the audio part is bound (AudioOut.write, tests/audio_run.py); file, e-ink and serial parts follow their slices. Slice 4d: SerialPort.write returns the bytes taken (at most 4096 a call); Eink.page/update/canvas().flush() return true (sent) or false (queued: the newest queued page is kept and sent when the panel limits allow).

entries.js: handle.close()
entries.test: host: stale generation after reopen; frame stays mapped after fb close
entries.notes: fb0 surface stays mapped until the program ends.

entries.js: not exposed raw; each request below has its own JS method
entries.test: host: unknown request ENOTTY per device kind
entries.notes: Request = class<<16 | op. Classes in use: 1 fb, 2 audio, 3 input, 4 eink, 6 serial (5 unused).

entries.js: ScreenLease.pixels: Uint32Array/Uint16Array/Uint8Array over the mapped surface; detached (length 0) at release
entries.test: host: wrong protection EACCES; anonymous mapping ENOSYS
entries.notes: Always maps the whole surface at 0x40000000; staying mapped after close means JS must never keep a view across a mode change.

entries.js: FileHandle.seek(position) -> position (0 to size)
entries.errors: ESPIPE (not a file), EINVAL (whence != 0 or offset < 0)
entries.test: tests/files_run.py: seek bounds
entries.notes: Absolute offsets only, read-only files; a position past the size is a RangeError before the kernel is asked.

entries.js: fs.readdir(path) -> names (8.3 as the card lists them)
entries.errors: ENOTDIR, EINVAL (buffer smaller than one entry)
entries.test: host: only if a profile needs 8.3 aliases
entries.notes: Plain readdir only; the long-name call is fs.readdir(path, {meta:true}).

entries.js: Writer.commit() (open, write, fsync, close in one step)
entries.test: host: dirty then clean commit; non-writer EINVAL
entries.notes: The runtime never holds a kernel writer open between JS calls, so a dropped or aborted writer costs the card nothing.

entries.js: sandbox.now() -> whole microseconds (a Number, exact); performance.now() (ms, since app start) as before
entries.test: host: monotonic, microsecond steps
entries.notes: No BigInt: a double holds microseconds exactly for 285 years.

entries.js: sandbox.sleep(ms) / sleep(ms) -> Promise; setTimeout as before; the loop sleeps at most 100 ms at a time (JSDEV_SLEEP_CHUNK_NS)
entries.test: host: past deadline returns at once; heartbeat still due while asleep
entries.notes: The heartbeat limit is 2 s and sleep does not service it, so the loop asks for the kernel sleep in chunks of at most 100 ms and calls the health call between them (G3).

entries.js: sys.exit(status) then return from the callback
entries.test: host: status values reach the supervisor; teardown closes every handle

entries.js: internal to the loop; apps cannot call it
entries.why: Hidden: the core guarantees the heartbeat; a script that blocks it is stopped by the execution budget (slice 5). Exposed only as sys.stats().healths read-only.
entries.test: host: loop heartbeats while idle and while in a 1 s busy script
entries.notes: Hidden: the core guarantees the heartbeat; a script that blocks it is stopped by the execution budget (slice 5). Exposed only as sys.stats().healths read-only.

entries.js: the 8.3 fallback of fs.stat when a long-name listing has no match
entries.test: host: dates decode to the FAT epoch
entries.notes: Used only inside fs.stat.

entries.errors: EINVAL (different folders), EBUSY (writer or cache reader open), ENAMETOOLONG
entries.test: host: cross-folder EINVAL; rename while a reader is open EBUSY
entries.notes: This is the only way to rename a file; there is no unlink (gap G2). The kernel's whole-file write already replaces a save in place (data first, then one directory entry).

entries.errors: ENOTDIR, ENOENT, EINVAL (buffer < 280 bytes for one entry)
entries.test: host: long names, non-ASCII names, entry that does not fit the buffer
entries.notes: Wrapper uses a 4 KiB buffer. modified and created are the FAT date and time words (opaque fingerprints).

entries.js: internal: the runtime asks for its heap block once at start; mem.arenaBytes read-only
entries.why: Hidden from apps: it is the runtime's own memory plan (2,195,456 bytes at 0x30000000, never executable). Apps see sys.memory().
entries.test: host: repeat request returns the same lease
entries.notes: Hidden from apps: it is the runtime's own memory plan (2,195,456 bytes at 0x30000000, never executable). Apps see sys.memory().

entries.js: power.hold(reason, {noBlank = true, noSlowdown = false}) -> Hold {release(), released, reason}; power.holds
entries.errors: EINVAL (no flags or unknown bits), EMFILE (-24, token table full), EOVERFLOW
entries.test: devices_run.py PowerTests
entries.notes: At most 16 holds (the kernel's table); EMFILE beyond. Every hold is given back at stop (reported in the log). The default holds no blank only.

entries.js: Hold.release() (twice is a no-op)
entries.test: devices_run.py PowerTests holds
entries.notes: The runtime keeps the token; an app cannot release one twice or one it does not own, so the kernel's EBADF/EINVAL are never seen.

entries.js: power.asleep -> {blank, slowdown}; power.screenDark; power.on('blank'|'wake', fn)
entries.errors: EINVAL on a kernel older than 1.12 -> treated as awake
entries.test: devices_run.py PowerTests PowerAudio
entries.notes: The loop looks at most every 100 ms and only while a listener or the audio pump needs it. While the screen is blank the audio pump does not synthesize or call onneed unless the app holds noBlank (the kernel drops audio then); it resumes on wake. screenDark is false while the app holds noBlank. An older kernel (EINVAL) is treated as lit.

entries.test: host: counters after partial write and underrun
entries.notes: Counters are per open. The runtime asks for the free room before each write and queues only that, so the kernel's overruns stay 0 and `refused` counts the short writes instead.

gaps.title: Input wait
gaps.problem: No blocking read or poll: input must be opened nonblocking and sleep_until does not wake on input. JS must poll between sleeps, costing latency or power. Slice 4b hides this in the runtime: input is polled every 10 ms (100 ms with no device), at most 128 events a turn; the cost is the wakeups, about 100 a second while idle.
gaps.proposal: A wake-on-input flag for sleep_until, or a blocking input read that still serves the heartbeat

gaps.title: Writing files
gaps.problem: Only whole-file WRONLY|CREAT|TRUNC to 8.3 names under CACHE or SAVES/GAME; no append, read-write, mkdir, unlink, stat, or writes elsewhere; 1 MiB per file held in kernel RAM; one writer. JS fs.writeFile and an OS that keeps its own data cannot be built on it. Slice 4a's JS file API is built on exactly this: reads with seek, whole-file staged writes to saves and the app's cache file.
gaps.proposal: unlink, mkdir, a per-OS data folder (for example /sd/OS/DATA/<OS>/), long names, append; see the slice 4a proposals G11 to G14

gaps.title: Heartbeat during sleeps
gaps.problem: sleep_until does not extend the heartbeat deadline and the allowed interval is not in the ABI. A long timer wait must be chopped into slices by the runtime. Slice 4b chops every wait into kernel sleeps of at most 100 ms (JSDEV_SLEEP_CHUNK_NS) and services the heartbeat between them; the 2 s limit is from docs/os-authors.md, not the ABI.
gaps.proposal: Publish the heartbeat limit in the startup record; let sleep_until count as progress up to it

gaps.title: Memory
gaps.problem: No anonymous mmap, free or resize; one 2,195,456-byte arena per run plus the ELF's own image (1 MiB ceiling). Typed arrays for images and sound compete for it.
gaps.proposal: A second arena or a resizable one (separately authorized)

gaps.title: Process model
gaps.problem: No exec or launch-next: switching apps means exiting back to the kernel or launcher, and the kernel passes no argv or app name. Today the convention is /OS/AUTORUN.TXT: the kernel reads line 1 (the ELF), JS.ELF reads line 2 (the app). That works for a boot-time app but not for one app starting another with an argument.
gaps.proposal: Keep the AUTORUN.TXT line-2 convention for v1; ask for a launch request with a short argument string only if app-to-app launch is needed

gaps.title: Text input
gaps.problem: The input queue carries key codes, no characters, layouts or composition. KeyboardEvent.key and typed text need a JS keymap that assumes a US layout.
gaps.proposal: Report the HID usage and modifier state, or the layout, to the OS

gaps.title: Entropy and wall time
gaps.problem: No random source and no real-time clock. Math.random needs a seed from boot jitter; Date is meaningless. Slice 4b seeds Math.random from the clock at app start, the startup record, 64 back-to-back clock reads and key timings as they come: little more than timer jitter, a handful of bits, never for secrets. sandbox.seed shows the seed; sandbox.seedRandom(n) makes a run reproducible.
gaps.proposal: getrandom-style call; optionally a time source or a way for the host to set it over USB

gaps.title: Audio feedback
gaps.problem: Write is nonblocking with a 341 ms ring and no wake on drain, and the rate is fixed at 48 kHz. A JS player must poll audio.stats() and schedule itself.
gaps.proposal: A blocking write or a readiness signal

gaps.title: Display sync
gaps.problem: FB_PRESENT is a synchronous copy; there is no vsync wait, page flip, or display-size query beyond the negotiated mode, so tearing and frame pacing are on the runtime.
gaps.proposal: Present-complete or vblank timestamp

gaps.title: Execution control
gaps.problem: No timer signal or preemption: a runaway script is stopped only by the interpreter's own interrupt hook in userland and the heartbeat watchdog in the kernel.
gaps.proposal: None needed; documented as the isolation limit of v1

gaps.title: No stat
gaps.problem: A file's size comes only from its parent folder's listing, which on a big folder (a games folder) costs a whole scan per fs.open or fs.stat.
gaps.proposal: a stat call by path, or the size in the open record's output

gaps.title: Writers cannot start from the old file
gaps.problem: Whole-file TRUNC writes mean an app that changes one byte of a 200 KiB save must keep the whole file in RAM and write all of it.
gaps.proposal: open for read-write on a save (copy-on-write), or an append flag, with the same fsync commit

gaps.title: A reader in the save area blocks commits
gaps.problem: Any open read handle on /OS/SAVES or /OS/CACHE (even a directory) makes a commit fail with EBUSY, so an app cannot stream-read one save while writing another.
gaps.proposal: block only a reader of the same file, or document a read-then-close rule as the contract (the JS runtime documents it today)

gaps.title: No remaining-space or quota query
gaps.problem: The kernel reports EDQUOT and ENOSPC only when a commit fails, so the JS quota (default 256 KiB per app) is a guess made in the runtime, and an app cannot ask how much card is left.
gaps.proposal: a query for free bytes and the used/limit counts of games and files in SAVES

gaps.title: No list of display modes
gaps.problem: The kernel documents a rule (width 16 to 1920 and a multiple of 4, height 16 to 1200, 1,228,800 bytes at most) but has no call that lists the modes, so screen.modes() offers common sizes that pass the rule and the firmware may still refuse one.
gaps.proposal: a query that returns the supported modes, or at least the rule and the display's native size

gaps.title: No input hot-plug notice and no event time
gaps.problem: The queue says nothing when the device goes away or comes back: the runtime infers a detach from a read error and tries to reopen every 100 ms. Events carry no timestamp, so the runtime stamps them when it reads (up to 10 ms late).
gaps.proposal: an attach/detach marker event on the queue, and a time field on each event

gaps.title: No vertical blank or present-complete
gaps.problem: A lease draws straight into the mapped surface and present() copies synchronously, so an app that animates cannot tell where the display is in its refresh and may tear.
gaps.proposal: a vblank timestamp or a present call that returns after the copy is on screen (extends G9)

gaps.title: No volume, mute, flush or tone call for apps
gaps.problem: The mixer's tone, tune and Q8 volume are kernel-internal (docs/audio-device.md slice 3) and close() is the only way to drop queued audio. The runtime therefore synthesizes square-wave tones itself, scales volume and mute in software on its own writes, and cannot cancel sound already in the ring (stop() only forgets tones not yet written; at most 200 ms stays queued).
gaps.proposal: an AUDIO ioctl for master volume and mute, a flush (drop queued frames), and optionally the mixer's tone and tune as a syscall

gaps.title: Audio counters are coarse and the rate is fixed
gaps.problem: AUDIO_QUERY does not expose the silence frames the ring counted, so an app sees underruns (one per dry millisecond tick) but not how long the gap was, and a lower rate costs the runtime a repeat loop. A player cannot learn that the screen is blanked (writes are dropped silently) except through power.asleep.
gaps.proposal: expose silence_frames and a dropped-while-blank counter in sbx_audio_info; optionally 24000 and 16000 Hz opens

gaps.title: No way to wait for or learn the e-ink and power limits, and the kernel keeps both after an app switch
gaps.problem: The e-ink panel answers EAGAIN with no hint of when it will take an update (the runtime paces by the reported 1 s and 30 a minute and retries every 250 ms), a clear at app stop may be refused as too soon (the page then stays up until the program ends), and power timeouts persist until the program ends, so power.setTimeouts is left unbound.
gaps.proposal: a retry-after in the EAGAIN reply or the info record, an e-ink clear that is not rate limited at an app boundary, and a way to restore the default power timeouts

gaps.title: Serial write takes everything and drops silently
gaps.problem: The kernel's write always reports every byte taken and counts what did not fit as dropped, so the runtime cannot return a short count the way audio does and an app learns of loss only from stats().txDropped; the host model takes only what fits to exercise the partial-write contract.
gaps.proposal: report the bytes queued (a short count or EAGAIN) so the app can wait for room
